title: Weaker Models
description:
**SITUATION:**

You are still on the **Fleetline** dispatch team.

**What the dispatch service is.** Dispatch is Fleetline's backend for trips. It is not the map, not payments, and not the driver chat. It is the service that **owns trip state**: who requested the ride, which driver was matched, and what step the trip is on right now.

ETA and "cars nearby" do not need linearizability. Stronger-than-needed models cost latency. The map can be a little stale; trip ownership cannot.

**YOUR TASK:**

Implement Lab 4.2 (`TODO(4.2)`).

1. Implement (or simulate) one weaker model for nearby-driver reads.
2. Show a history that is legal under that model but illegal under linearizability — and argue why that is OK for the map.
3. Keep ownership on the strong API from 4.1.

**SPEC:**

- Nearby API uses the weaker model
- At least one history distinguishes weak vs linearizable
- Ownership path unchanged
- Document the model name in the solution notes

> **Note:** Graded Submit for this lab is not live yet. Use **Run** in the editor when verify commands exist; otherwise read the brief and explore the starter. The harness lands next.

hints: Map refresh every second cannot pay quorum latency every time.
Show a history legal under weak but illegal under linearizability.
Name the model you chose (sequential, causal, …).
problemStatement.overview: Nearby drivers do not need linearizability; pick a weaker model and defend it.
problemStatement.brief: Implement a weaker consistency model for nearby-driver reads.
